prompt: how do large language models like ChatGPT work

plan.title: How ChatGPT Works: Predicting the Next Word
plan.description: Large language models like ChatGPT generate text by predicting one word piece at a time. This video explains tokens, training on text, and why the answers can sound right and still be wrong.

beats.narration: ChatGPT does not look up answers. It does one thing, over and over: it guesses the next word. That single trick, repeated thousands of times, writes essays, code, and poems.

props.text: It just predicts the next word. Again and again.

beats.narration: First, text is chopped into small pieces called tokens. Then the model reads a huge amount of writing and practices guessing what comes next. Each miss nudges its internal settings, so the next guess improves.
When you type a prompt, the model scores every possible next token and picks one likely choice. It adds that token to the text, then repeats. Your answer is built piece by piece.

Because it predicts what sounds likely, not what is verified, it can state something false with total confidence. Fluent does not mean correct. So treat answers as a strong draft, and check the facts that matter.

props.verdict: Fluent is not the same as correct
